title: How pollination works
source: A short schematic lesson; review against your curriculum before publication.

scenes.title: From anther to stigma
scenes.narration: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma.

segments.narration: Anthers produce pollen. During pollination, pollen is transferred to a stigma.
segments.visual: Schematic transfer between two flowers. Keep source and destination visible.

shot.heading: Pollination: from anther to stigma
shot.learning_objective: Identify the source and destination of pollen.

scenes.title: The order matters
scenes.narration: Compare two sequences of reproductive timing.

segments.narration: In protandry, anthers release pollen first. Later, the stigma becomes receptive.
segments.visual: Keep one schematic flower visible while highlighting the two stages.

shot.heading: Protandry: pollen first
shot.learning_objective: Recognize pollen release before stigma receptivity.

segments.narration: In protogyny, the stigma becomes receptive first. Later, anthers release pollen.
segments.visual: Reverse the two stages on the same schematic flower.

shot.heading: Protogyny: receptive stigma first
shot.learning_objective: Recognize stigma receptivity before pollen release.

segments.narration: Protandry means pollen is released first. Protogyny means the stigma becomes receptive first.
segments.visual: Two comparison cards highlight in narration order.
